# Sidebar

The side navigation of an app, open while people work.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-sidebar--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:light" title="Sidebar examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-sidebar--docs">Open Sidebar in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-sidebar--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Account area navigation.

- **Use it when:** Apps with several sections people move between all session.
- **Not when:** A website's main navigation (navigation menu), or a few sections that fit in tabs.

Instead:

- [Navigation menu](./navigation-menu.md): Website navigation.
- [Tabs](./tabs.md): Views of one thing.

## Why it works this way

Sidebar looks the way it does because of 2 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Sidebar, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-theming-definition"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How are brands handled?</b><code>theming.definition</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Brands as modes</div><p>Brands are theme modes over shared semantics.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Sidebar</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Account-area menu items, the same in every brand.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>outline</b>: Brands change color and corners, not the structure of the menu.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Empty: default</code> <code>Item: muted</code> <code>Toggle: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Sidebar decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-spacing-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many densities exist?</b><code>spacing.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One</div><p>One density across brands.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Sidebar</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Every account-area menu item.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>sm</b>: One density across brands.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>lg</b>: One density across brands.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Item: sm</code> <code>Toggle: lg</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Sidebar decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is a navigation landmark; the current section is marked; collapsing keeps names for icons. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add sidebar
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Sidebar reads 122 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Sidebar's tokens to change Sidebar alone.
